translations.title: The first-timer's home loan checklist
translations.excerpt: Twelve things to settle before you sign, from the EMI ceiling to the prepayment clause.

blocks.text: A home loan is the largest financial commitment most families ever make, and the paperwork arrives faster than the thinking. Work through this list before the sanction letter, not after.

items: Keep the EMI under 35% of take-home pay, including any existing EMIs.
Have the down payment (20% or more) plus registration and stamp duty in a separate account; do not borrow it.
Keep a six-month emergency fund outside the down payment.
Check your credit score; above 750 usually gets the lowest rate band.
Decide the tenure with the EMI calculator: a shorter tenure costs more each month but far less overall.
Floating rate linked to an external benchmark (repo rate), with the spread written down.
No prepayment or foreclosure penalty on floating-rate loans to individuals; this is the rule, confirm it is in writing.
Processing fee, legal and valuation charges listed with amounts.
What happens to the EMI when rates change: the tenure usually stretches first; ask for the EMI to rise instead if you can afford it.
Term life cover for at least the loan amount, bought separately rather than bundled.
Set up the EMI auto-debit two days after salary day.
Prepay one extra EMI a year if you can; on a 20-year loan it removes roughly three years.
Keep the interest certificate for tax: up to {section_80c_limit} of principal under 80C and home-loan interest under 24(b) in the old regime.
EMI under 35% of take-home, emergency fund intact, down payment unborrowed.
Floating rate, benchmark-linked, no prepayment penalty, all in writing.
One extra EMI a year shortens the loan by years.
